items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: And then he played with George Williams, big George Williams.

ctx.x: Yeah, I heard talk about him.

Oh, yeah. He used to play with people. And then he played with us. And then he played with George Williams, big George Williams. Then he had a band, you know. Boy, he played with Peerrell until Peerrell died. Then after that, he didn't spend with anybody, you know. Work all the time. He was a printer, you know. Played music at night. He was a heavy drinker. He was the finest man in one of me. He didn't look at him up there. I used to play with him sometimes too. Me and him and Eddie Hickman. Three piece. He could…

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: And then they had big George Williams with us, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah, playing piano with a thing, you know. And then they had big George Williams with us, you know. You know him, George Williams? Played drums. Played drums? Yeah, he was playing with I-tay, you know, about a couple of weeks ago.
Did he have a bass player?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: He had Bill Matthews and George Williams.

ctx.x: Ask him what Bottler's name was.

He said, what's Bottler's name was? I forget his first name. That's his last name, Bottler. And he was playing with us with our tape, you know. And, uh, and I tell you, he got rid of him. And he got washed, you see. And then, uh, you know, until I got down there, they tried to let them band stay on the job too long, you see. So, he's a different man, you know. Like that. That's what I tell you about, about a month ago now. He had to tell you, man. He had Bill Matthews and George Williams. And two more other…
Thomas Jefferson's in on the trumpet.
